topic: AI literacy is now one of the hardest skills to hire for
post:
The hardest skill to hire for right now isn't coding. 👀
It's knowing how to actually use AI at work.

ManpowerGroup surveyed 39,000 employers across 41 countries.
For the first time, AI skills topped the list of hardest-to-find skills:

🧠 AI model & app development: 20%
📚 AI literacy: 19%

That second one is the opportunity.
AI literacy doesn't need a computer science degree. It means you can:

✅ Write clear prompts and give AI the right context
✅ Check AI output instead of trusting it blindly
✅ Spot which parts of your job AI can speed up
✅ Use it safely with company data

Why it matters:
This week's reporting on the "AI career premium" points the same way: people who can apply AI to real work are moving ahead faster.

Practical takeaway:
Pick one weekly task this week, like a report, a summary or a status email.
Do it with AI, check every fact, and write down what worked.
That's a real, provable skill you can talk about in your next review or interview.

What's one task you've already handed to AI? 👇

Follow for daily AI news.
